newsitem.title: THAILAND: Queen Elizabeth arrives for five-day Thai visit.
newsitem.headline: Queen Elizabeth arrives for five-day Thai visit.

text.p: Britain's Queen Elizabeth and her husband Prince Philip arrived in Thailand on Monday for a five-day visit to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Thai King Bhumibol Adulyadej's accession to the throne.
The queen, on her second visit to Thailand, was given a ceremonial welcome at the airport by the King and later presented with the keys to the city at a pavilion in the centre of Bangkok.
"We are very pleased to be paying a return visit to your hospitable city," she said, noting the Thai capital had changed "almost beyond recognition" since she and Prince Philip first visited in 1972.
"The city has experienced great economic development over the last quarter of a century," said the queen, who was dressed in a bright green dress and hat, and black gloves.
The British monarch sailed through Bangkok's usually traffic-clogged streets, as police escorted her royal motorcade through the Union-Jack-lined city.
But other traffic was jammed up for miles on portions of the expressway leading to the airport as police blocked access until the queen had passed, witnesses said.
Queen Elizabeth is in Thailand as a guest of King Bhumibol, the world's longest-reigning monarch.
Among a host of other functions, she is due to meet caretaker prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa and travel to the ancient Thai capital of Ayudhya during her visit.
